task.description: WF-05 step 3, SECURITY-AUDITOR, dimension «security» of the part `pixel-office`, audit AUD-002 (run AUD-002-20261122-01). SCOPE. Security of Pixel Office (tools/src/pixel-office: 33 own files, 17462 lines; the band Critical: ISS-0092 is about this part first, DEP-01). Changed since AUD-001: server.js (reads only with a key, ISS-0122; a signed body once, ISS-0123), hook.sh (82 lines), main.js, note.js, protocol.js, mask.js (ISS-0121, findSecrets of REQ-102), public/app.js, office-report.js, texts.js. EXTRA CHECKS. (1) R2 and the write permissions: search the whole project (not only this folder) for any code or script that writes Pixel Office events outside the hook and the signed note path; none may exist; the page code (public/) must contain no write request (2) whether /bin/sh hook.sh runs on this Windows PC is not measured (scout issue I8): read it, do not run it; never bind, probe or stop ports 4780 and 4790 (3) fixtures with secrets: tools/test/fixtures/pixel-office must hold only fake values NEEDS. NOT ALLOWED. On this PC: run npm run check, any npm script of tools/ or app/ that runs tests, node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; start Chrome; bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790; edit any project file other than your own report; commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. Write your report to the file named in `output` (create the folder; JSON, 2-space indent, LF) as an object {audit:'AUD-002', part, dimension, role, subject:'f72eaa7', checked:[{check, how (the command or the files read), result}], not_checked:[{check, why}], findings:[...], summary}. A finding has the fields of WF-05 step 3: id (a short code like SEC-APP-01), check (what was checked; for requirements the requirement id and the criterion), severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low by WF-05 step 3), title, where (file and line), evidence (the command and its output, or a quote: a finding without evidence is not written), item (the bar item Q/R), recommendation (what exactly to fix and in which files). Severity by WF-05: Critical = a violation of a bar item that harms already now (a secret in files, invented events in Pixel Office, mixing of customer data, writing outside the own folder); High = a bar item not met or a criterion of a `done` requirement no longer met or a divergence from a recorded decision or a dependency with a known vulnerability; Medium = a document diverges from the files, a weak test, an outdated dependency without a known vulnerability; Low = names, dead code, formatting. Do not report a place that an open defect in docs/issues/ already covers: name the defect in `checked` instead. Do not pad: only real, evidenced findings; report what you could NOT check with the reason (this is not a finding and not a pass). In the `result` of your handoff write: verdict COMPLETED, the path of the report, the counts of findings by severity, the number of checks done and not done, and `issues` for anything ORCH or the owner must decide. The audit changes nothing in the project: your only files are the report and the result of your handoff. BE ECONOMICAL: the owner's usage limit is real.
